items.title: El Salvador president says bodies found in Haiti are not those of hostages
items.description: Nayib Bukele says bodies delivered to soldiers are "not our men" amid search for Salvadorans abducted last week.

items.title: Why is Egypt so wary of getting involved in Yemen’s conflict?
items.description: As Egypt considers defending Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks, memories of its war in Yemen in the 1960s loom large.

items.title: Israeli soldiers raze neighbourhood in Hebron, driving families from homes
items.description: PM Benjamin Netanyahu vows ‘to destroy this place’ in retaliation for militant attack on army checkpointIsraeli troops have levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in collective punishment for a militant attack on an army checkpoint outside the West Bank city, local Palestinian authorities …

items.title: 'Donald Trump goes further than the eccentric scientist from 'Honey, I Shrunk the Kids.' He is shrinking America'
items.description: The US president's decision to assist Vladimir Putin in his war against Ukraine – most notably with the diesel fuel deal – marks the latest chapter in his ongoing campaign to dismantle America's superpower status, analyzes Le Monde columnist Alain Frachon.

items.title: Trump, 'faremo affari con Russia e Ucraina una volta finita la guerra'
Thousands take to Tel Aviv's streets for protests against Netanyahu
items.description: Thousands marched against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government in Tel Aviv on Saturday – just three days before Israel's general election – demanding accountability for the failure to prevent a Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, that led to the war in Gaza.

items.title: Police and protesters clash in Paris as demonstrations break out across Europe
items.description: Demonstrations rocked many European cities Saturday, from Milan to Madrid. The protests encompass a broad range of issues, from education to housing.

items.title: Women ‘first to suffer’ under siege, first to step up as frontline responders in Sudan
items.description: When Tahani Al-Numeiri heard the first explosions in Khartoum, her hometown, war seemed so remote that she assumed they were celebrations from a nearby wedding. It was the morning of 15 April 2023, and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces had just turned their guns on the army.

items.title: Drinking water supplies dwindle in Yemeni city besieged by Houthi rebels
items.description: Taiz, a city in southwestern Yemen, faces a severe water crisis as Houthi rebels backed by Iran tighten their encirclement. The city has struggled with water issues for over a decade, but the situation has worsened in recent weeks.

items.title: Zelensky Ready to Freeze Front Line to Halt War, Rejects Land Cession
items.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is prepared to freeze combat operations along existing front lines to bring an immediate halt to the war, while firmly rejecting territorial concessions and vowing never to recognize occupied lands as Russian sovereign territory. items.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
items.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

items.title: Every Day We 'Wake Up Poorer': Iranians Battle Economic Woes
items.description: Battered by mismanagement, sanctions, and war, Iran’s economy is in deep trouble. The cost-of-living crisis is forcing people to change what they eat, how they socialize, and what they can afford to do with their lives.

items.title: Putin Says Renewed Peace Talks Must Focus on Security for Russia, Ukraine and Europe Overall
items.description: The president said that Russia remains intent on resolving the conflict once and for all rather than agreeing to a short-lived ceasefire with Kyiv.
